## Approach re-analysis (2026-05-29)

**Option 2 (two-phase sync: inbound-first then refresh+outbound) is REJECTED — breaks local label removal.**

Scenario: local=[A, X], jira=[A, X, dso-id]. User removes X locally → local=[A].
- Inbound runs first against pre-pass snapshot: emits ADD X, applies → local=[A, X]
- Refresh: local=[A, X], jira=[A, X] → outbound emits nothing
- Net: X silently restored locally; user's removal undone.

The PR #457 local-wins suppression is load-bearing precisely because neither differ has a baseline. Reordering does not add information — it inverts which side wins by default.

**Only options 1 and 3 are correct fixes** (both add a baseline so differs can distinguish "local never had X" from "local had X and removed it"):

- **Option 1 — local-intent tracking**: outbound only emits REMOVE when there's a corresponding local TAG_REMOVE event. Requires consuming the event log in outbound_differ (larger surface).
- **Option 3 — binding-time baseline (RECOMMENDED)**: snapshot local tags at bind time, store on binding record. Outbound differ computes diff against (current_local - baseline) intent, suppressing spurious REMOVEs for labels local never had. Smaller schema delta than option 1; preserves local-wins semantics; no orchestration reorder needed.

Updated recommendation: **option 3**. Awaiting user approval before implementation.
